newsitem.title: UK: BA drive could cost 5,000 jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA drive could cost 5,000 jobs - paper.

text.p: British Airways Plc chief executive Robert Ayling will on Wednesday tell senior airline managers that around 5,000 jobs could be lost as part of the carrier's efficiency drive, the Times newspaper said.
A British Airways spokeswoman, speaking by telephone, confirmed Ayling would be talking to staff at Heathrow on Wednesday, but declined to comment on possible job cuts.

The "Step Change" efficiency drive aims to cut a billion stg from the carrier's annual cost base before the year 2000. The Times said Ayling would tell managers that rising costs and increased competition meant a reorganisation of the airline was inevitable.

British Airways would also create a new intra-European network from next April and form an alliance with a major Far Eastern airline that would take three years to be fully implemented, the paper said.
Ayling said earlier this year that management was looking at areas where it might consider buying in services if they were cheaper than in-house operations.
